svg.title: Developer workflow for the Foundry Dispatch Advisor
svg.desc: Left to right. Git branch feature/lesson99-dispatch-advisor holds the agent definition as code: instructions.md, the tool specifications, the ranker, the guard, the facts snapshot and the evaluation set. Stage 1, pull request build, needs no Azure: 17 pytest cases and the evaluation-set check against the ranker. Stage 2, after merge, in project cedar-agents of cedar-ai-dev: ensure_agent creates a new immutable version only when the definition fingerprint changed, otherwise reuses the latest version. Stage 3, cloud evaluation gate: Foundry sends the 14 evaluation queries to that version and scores them with tool_call_accuracy, tool_selection and tool_input_accuracy; each must pass at 0.9 or more, otherwise the pipeline stops. Stage 4, the same code runs against the test project in cedar-ai-test, creating the agent there from the same definition; nothing is exported or imported. Lina reviews the bands with Sami before release 2. Below: the portal playground is used for exploring and its changes are copied back into Git; a version created by hand is not trusted by the pipeline because its fingerprint does not match.
svg.text: From Git to a gated agent version in each Foundry project
• The playground is for exploring. A change that works there is copied into Git and released by the pipeline.
• A version created by hand has no matching fingerprint, so the next pipeline run creates a fresh version from Git.
• Function tools run in the host, so the cloud gate scores tool choice and arguments; the answers are checked by the guard.
• Each project gets its own agent and agent identity; roles are assigned per project, never copied.
• Rollback = point callers at an earlier version, which is still there because versions are immutable.
